Clarity.justification: The paper is exceptionally well-structured with clear sections (Abstract, Introduction, Related Work, Method, Experiments, Results, Discussion, Conclusion). Ideas are articulated logically and concisely, with explicit hypotheses, layer-sweep tables, and baseline comparisons. Minor deduction for occasional repetition of AUROC numbers across sections.

Novelty.justification: The core idea of linear probing hidden states for correctness builds directly on prior work (Burns et al. 2023, Kossen et al. 2024, logit lens). The inverted-U layer pattern and single-pass 0.885 AUROC are incremental contributions rather than groundbreaking; the paper itself notes alignment with Aiersilan et al. (2026) and does not claim architectural novelty.

Soundness.justification: Experimental results are fully consistent with the provided code and logs: layer-15 AUROC 0.852 (sweep) and 0.885 (full data), token-entropy baseline 0.623, inverted-U pattern verified, all gates passed, and hook non-intrusiveness confirmed. Minor issues include reduced sample size for the layer sweep and three untested predictions listed in limitations; no evidence of fabricated data.

Significance.justification: The work addresses a practically important problem (efficient hallucination detection) and demonstrates a deployable single-pass method. Impact is tempered by restriction to one model family, English QA only, and exact-match labeling; broader validation would be needed for lasting field impact.

strengths: Clear, reproducible experimental pipeline with code matching reported numbers
Systematic layer-depth analysis confirming inverted-U pattern
weaknesses: Incremental novelty relative to existing probing and semantic-entropy literature
Limited scope (single model, English QA, exact-match labels) reduces generalizability
